sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Termination clause — 'reasonable notice' clearly define nahi hai.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Define an agreed written notice period (such as 60 or 90 days as a negotiated commercial benchmark) and specify conditions under which either party can terminate.
sample_1_commercial_lease.legal_basis: Contract Act 1872 (Sections 39, 73) & Provincial Rented Premises Legislation

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: The clause does not clearly distinguish structural repairs from routine tenant upkeep, which may create disputes. Clarify the respective responsibilities of both parties.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Clarify that landlord maintains structural integrity and external premises, while tenant handles internal minor operational upkeep.
sample_1_commercial_lease.legal_basis: Provincial Rented Premises Legislation (Punjab 2009 / Sindh 1979) – Statutory Maintenance Allocation

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Late payment — late fee/penalty ya exact consequences specified nahi.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Define a clear grace period and applicable consequences to avoid arbitrary dispute or undefined penalties.
sample_1_commercial_lease.legal_basis: Contract Act 1872 (Section 74 - Liquidated damages & penalty limits)

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Renewal — renewal terms, notice period aur revised rent ka mechanism missing hai.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Add clause defining an agreed/negotiated renewal mechanism and clear notice window prior to lease expiry.
sample_1_commercial_lease.legal_basis: Provincial Rented Premises Legislation & Contract Act 1872

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Notices — exact notice method/address/timeframe clearly specified nahi.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: State that notices must be served via registered courier or official designated business email addresses.

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Insurance — required insurance coverage/type/party responsibility clearly defined nahi.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Clarify that building fire/structure insurance rests with landlord; internal business contents rest with tenant.

sample_1_commercial_lease.expected_issue: Tax considerations — agreement mein applicable withholding tax treatment ka specific handling mention nahi hai.
sample_1_commercial_lease.suggested_action: Add explicit clause clarifying whether the agreed rent is gross or net of statutory withholding deductions where the payer is a prescribed withholding agent under prevailing tax law.
sample_1_commercial_lease.legal_basis: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Section 155 - Deduction of Tax on Rent)

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Missing concrete deliverables, milestones, and acceptance criteria.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: Attach a detailed Statement of Work (SOW) defining milestones and sign-off criteria.

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Vendor has unilateral right to revise charges whenever additional work or circumstances require it.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: Require a formal written change-order signed by both parties before any additional fee can be charged.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.legal_basis: Contract Act 1872 & ITO 2001 (Section 153 - Prescribed Withholding Requirements)

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Vague delivery timeline ('reasonable efforts within an appropriate timeframe').
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: Specify concrete milestone dates and define what constitutes an excusable vs unexcusable delay.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.legal_basis: Contract Act 1872 (Section 55 - Time as essence of contract)

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Client only receives right to use materials; ownership of custom deliverables remains unallocated.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: As a contractual option, specify that bespoke source code, designs, and deliverables are assigned to Client upon full payment, with vendor retaining pre-existing tools.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.legal_basis: Copyright Ordinance 1962 (Section 13) & IPO-Pakistan – Ownership and assignment of bespoke deliverables

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Liability capped at an ambiguous 'amount considered reasonable in the circumstances'.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: Define an explicit agreed liability cap and clear exclusions/carve-outs (such as gross negligence or confidentiality breach).

sample_2_vendor_agreement.expected_issue: Vendor can subcontract work to third parties without client prior notice or consent.
sample_2_vendor_agreement.suggested_action: Require prior written consent from Client before subcontracting core services.
